articles.title: Moving to Ireland from the US
articles.appTitle: Moving to Ireland from the US
articles.note: Visa-free entry, permits and Stamp 0, no licence exchange, tax treaty and 1993 social security agreement.
articles.description: Census 2022 counted 13,412 US citizens living in Ireland, up 27.5% on 2016, plus another 30,044 people holding dual Irish and American citizenship…
articles.previewHtml:
Census 2022 counted 13,412 US citizens living in Ireland, up 27.5% on 2016, plus another 30,044 people holding dual Irish and American citizenship. Americans come for tech and pharma jobs in Dublin, Cork and Galway, for university, to retire, or because a parent or grandparent was born here and an Irish passport is within reach. Ireland is English speaking, in the EU, and Dublin and Shannon both have US pre-clearance, so flying home is easy. The catch is that being American does not give you any right to live here, so the paperwork needs to be sorted before you pack.

Quick factsUS to Ireland
Visa to enterNo, up to 90 days
Permission to stay beyond 90 daysYes, needs a permit or scheme
US licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementYes
Social security agreementYes (1993)
US citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)13,412 (plus 30,044 dual)

Do you need a visa?

US citizens are not visa required, so you can enter Ireland for up to 90 days without applying for anything. Staying longer is a different matter: you need an immigration permission, and you must register it with Immigration Service Delivery within 90 days of arriving. The main routes are:
articles.gatedHtml:
• Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list (from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro, or 68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Spouses and partners can join you and work on Stamp 1G without their own permit.
  • General Employment Permit for most other jobs, minimum salary 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after a labour market needs test.
  • Working Holiday Authorisation for US citizens who are enrolled in full time third level education or graduated within the last 12 months. It lets you live and work in Ireland for up to 12 months and you do not need a job offer first.
  • Stamp 0 for retirees and people of independent means. You must show income of around 50,000 euro a year per person, hold private medical insurance, and you cannot work. Time on Stamp 0 does not count towards citizenship.
  • Family routes if you are joining an Irish or EU citizen spouse or partner.

If you have an Irish born grandparent, look at the Foreign Births Register before anything else. Once registered you are an Irish citizen and none of the above applies.

Your driving licence

The US is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you cannot swap a US licence for an Irish one. You can drive on your US licence for up to 12 months as a visitor, but once you are resident you must go through the Irish process: pass the driver theory test, get a learner permit, complete Essential Driver Training and pass the driving test. The good news is that experienced foreign licence holders only need 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and can skip the usual six month wait before the test.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and the US have a double taxation agreement, so income taxed in one country is generally credited in the other. As a US citizen you still file a US return every year, plus an FBAR if your foreign accounts exceed 10,000 dollars in total. Irish banks report US account holders to Revenue under FATCA, so be upfront about your citizenship when opening accounts.

There is a bilateral social security agreement in force since 1 September 1993. It lets you combine US Social Security credits with Irish PRSI contributions to qualify for a pension in either country, and US Social Security retirement benefits can be paid to you in Ireland.

Your US credit history does not transfer. Ireland's Central Credit Register only holds Irish borrowing, so you start from zero. Open an Irish bank account (you will need proof of an Irish address) and use a specialist transfer service rather than a bank wire for large dollar to euro transfers.

Healthcare

Once the HSE accepts you as ordinarily resident (living here or intending to live here for at least a year) you can use the public system. Public hospital inpatient charges were abolished in April 2023, but GP visits cost roughly 50 to 70 euro unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card on income grounds. Most Americans buy private health insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health for faster access. Buy it within 9 months of arriving: if you are 35 or older and wait longer, a Lifetime Community Rating loading is added to your premium.

Bringing your things and your pet

You can import your household goods free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for at least 12 months and owned the items for at least 6 months. File form C&E 1076 with Revenue.

The US is a listed country for pet travel, so your dog or cat does not need a rabies blood test. It needs an ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination given after the chip, an EU animal health certificate endorsed by USDA APHIS, tapeworm treatment for dogs, and you must give the Department of Agriculture advance notice so a compliance check can be done on arrival.

First 30 days checklist

  1. Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie. You need it for work, tax and healthcare.
  2. Register your immigration permission and get your IRP card (300 euro) within 90 days if you are staying beyond a visit.
  3. Open an Irish bank account and tell your employer your PPS number so you are not on emergency tax.
  4. Register with a GP near where you live and decide on private health insurance.
  5. Get a Leap card for buses, Luas and DART.

★ Useful links

  • Immigration Service Delivery
  • Employment permits (Department of Enterprise)
  • National Driver Licence Service
  • Revenue: double taxation treaties
  • Foreign Births Register

articles.title: Moving to Ireland from the UK
articles.appTitle: Moving to Ireland from the UK
articles.note: Common Travel Area rights, no visa or IRP, licence exchange, NHS to HSE and UK pension paid in Ireland.
articles.description: UK citizens are the second largest non-Irish group in the country. Census 2022 counted 83,347 UK citizens living in Ireland, and a further 31,907 people…
articles.previewHtml:
UK citizens are the second largest non-Irish group in the country. Census 2022 counted 83,347 UK citizens living in Ireland, and a further 31,907 people with dual Irish and UK citizenship. People move for work in Dublin's tech and finance sectors, to be closer to family, to study, or simply because the Common Travel Area makes it the easiest international move a British citizen can make. This guide covers what changes and what does not.

Quick factsUK to Ireland
Visa to enterNo
Permission to stay or workNot needed (Common Travel Area)
Immigration registration (IRP)Not needed for British citizens
UK licence exchangeableYes
Double taxation agreementYes
Social security agreementYes (Convention on Social Security)
UK citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)83,347

Do you need a visa?

No. Under the Common Travel Area, British citizens can live, work, study and retire in Ireland without a visa, residence permit or employment permit. Brexit did not change this. You do not register with Immigration Service Delivery, you do not get an IRP card, and there is no salary threshold or job offer requirement. You can also vote in Dáil and local elections once you are on the electoral register, though not in presidential elections or referendums.
articles.gatedHtml:
Two things to watch. First, the rights apply to British citizens, not to everyone who lives in the UK. A non-British family member (for example a spouse with Indian or Nigerian citizenship) needs their own Irish permission, usually through the family reunification route, and may need a visa to enter. Second, if you were born in Northern Ireland or have an Irish parent or grandparent, you may already be entitled to Irish citizenship, which is worth claiming for EU free movement.

Your driving licence

The UK is on the NDLS list of recognised states, so a full UK licence (including Northern Ireland) can be exchanged for an Irish one with no theory or driving test. Visitors can drive on a UK licence, but once you live in Ireland you must exchange it rather than keep driving on it. Apply online at ndls.ie if you have a Public Services Card and MyGovID, or book an NDLS centre appointment. Bring the licence, proof of your PPS number, proof of address and photo ID. The fee is 65 euro (free if you are 70 or over).

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and the UK have a long standing double taxation agreement. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a tax year (or 280 days over two years), and the treaty decides which country taxes what. Tell HMRC you are leaving (form P85) and register with Revenue using myAccount.

The Convention on Social Security between Ireland and the UK, in force since 1 January 2021, preserves the pre-Brexit position: you are covered by one country's system at a time, your UK National Insurance record and Irish PRSI record can be combined to qualify for a State Pension, and your UK State Pension is paid in Ireland with annual increases. UK workplace and personal pensions can generally stay where they are; transfers to Irish schemes are possible but need advice.

Your UK credit history does not follow you. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so expect to build a record from scratch before a mortgage or car loan. Sterling to euro transfers are cheapest through a specialist provider.

Healthcare

The Common Travel Area also protects healthcare rights, but the systems are different. The NHS is free at the point of use; the HSE is not. Once you are ordinarily resident (living in Ireland or intending to for at least a year) you can use public hospitals as a public patient, and inpatient charges were abolished in April 2023. A GP visit costs roughly 50 to 70 euro unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card on income grounds, and prescriptions are paid for up to a monthly cap under the Drugs Payment Scheme. Around half the population holds private health insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health. If you are 35 or older, buy it within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading. A UK GHIC covers you on visits, not as a resident.

Bringing your things and your pet

Since Brexit, goods arriving from Great Britain are imports from outside the EU. You can bring your household belongings free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for at least 12 months and owned the goods for at least 6 months; your removals company will file the declaration. Goods from Northern Ireland move freely. Cars registered in the UK must be registered for VRT within 30 days of arrival; relief is available if you owned the car for over 6 months abroad.

Pets from Great Britain need a microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, an EU animal health certificate issued by a vet within 10 days of travel, and tapeworm treatment for dogs. Pets from Northern Ireland travel with no extra checks.

First 30 days checklist

  1. Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie with your passport and proof of Irish address.
  2. No IRP is needed. Instead, register with Revenue myAccount once you have a PPS number so your employer can tax you correctly.
  3. Open an Irish bank account; a utility bill or tenancy agreement usually counts as proof of address.
  4. Register with a GP and, if you want it, buy private health insurance within 9 months.
  5. Get a Leap card for public transport and exchange your driving licence at the NDLS.

articles.plainText:
UK citizens are the second largest non-Irish group in the country. Census 2022 counted 83,347 UK citizens living in Ireland, and a further 31,907 people with dual Irish and UK citizenship. People move for work in Dublin's tech and finance sectors, to be closer to family, to study, or simply because the Common Travel Area makes it the easiest international move a British citizen can make. This guide covers what changes and what does not.

Quick factsUK to IrelandVisa to enterNoPermission to stay or workNot needed (Common Travel Area)Immigration registration (IRP)Not needed for British citizensUK licence exchangeableYesDouble taxation agreementYesSocial security agreementYes (Convention on Social Security)UK citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)83,347

Do you need a visa?

No. Under the Common Travel Area, British citizens can live, work, study and retire in Ireland without a visa, residence permit or employment permit. Brexit did not change this. You do not register with Immigration Service Delivery, you do not get an IRP card, and there is no salary threshold or job offer requirement. You can also vote in Dáil and local elections once you are on the electoral register, though not in presidential elections or referendums.

Two things to watch. First, the rights apply to British citizens, not to everyone who lives in the UK. A non-British family member (for example a spouse with Indian or Nigerian citizenship) needs their own Irish permission, usually through the family reunification route, and may need a visa to enter. Second, if you were born in Northern Ireland or have an Irish parent or grandparent, you may already be entitled to Irish citizenship, which is worth claiming for EU free movement.

Your driving licence

The UK is on the NDLS list of recognised states, so a full UK licence (including Northern Ireland) can be exchanged for an Irish one with no theory or driving test. Visitors can drive on a UK licence, but once you live in Ireland you must exchange it rather than keep driving on it. Apply online at ndls.ie if you have a Public Services Card and MyGovID, or book an NDLS centre appointment. Bring the licence, proof of your PPS number, proof of address and photo ID. The fee is 65 euro (free if you are 70 or over).

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and the UK have a long standing double taxation agreement. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a tax year (or 280 days over two years), and the treaty decides which country taxes what. Tell HMRC you are leaving (form P85) and register with Revenue using myAccount.

The Convention on Social Security between Ireland and the UK, in force since 1 January 2021, preserves the pre-Brexit position: you are covered by one country's system at a time, your UK National Insurance record and Irish PRSI record can be combined to qualify for a State Pension, and your UK State Pension is paid in Ireland with annual increases. UK workplace and personal pensions can generally stay where they are; transfers to Irish schemes are possible but need advice.

Your UK credit history does not follow you. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so expect to build a record from scratch before a mortgage or car loan. Sterling to euro transfers are cheapest through a specialist provider.

Healthcare

The Common Travel Area also protects healthcare rights, but the systems are different. The NHS is free at the point of use; the HSE is not. Once you are ordinarily resident (living in Ireland or intending to for at least a year) you can use public hospitals as a public patient, and inpatient charges were abolished in April 2023. A GP visit costs roughly 50 to 70 euro unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card on income grounds, and prescriptions are paid for up to a monthly cap under the Drugs Payment Scheme. Around half the population holds private health insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health. If you are 35 or older, buy it within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading. A UK GHIC covers you on visits, not as a resident.

Bringing your things and your pet

Since Brexit, goods arriving from Great Britain are imports from outside the EU. You can bring your household belongings free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for at least 12 months and owned the goods for at least 6 months; your removals company will file the declaration. Goods from Northern Ireland move freely. Cars registered in the UK must be registered for VRT within 30 days of arrival; relief is available if you owned the car for over 6 months abroad.

Pets from Great Britain need a microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, an EU animal health certificate issued by a vet within 10 days of travel, and tapeworm treatment for dogs. Pets from Northern Ireland travel with no extra checks.

articles.title: Moving to Ireland from India
articles.note: D visa and Critical Skills permits, Stamp 1G for family, non-exchangeable licence, tax treaty but no pension deal.

Census 2022 counted 45,449 Indian citizens living in Ireland, and in the year before the census alone 10,593 Indian citizens arrived, a 315% increase on 2016. The draw is clear: English speaking, EU based, and full of employers in software, pharma, medicine, nursing and finance who sponsor employment permits. This guide walks through the practical steps.

Quick factsIndia to Ireland
Visa to enterYes (long stay D visa)
Registration after arrivalYes, IRP within 90 days
Indian licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementYes
Social security agreementNo
Indian citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)45,449

articles.gatedHtml:
• Critical Skills Employment Permit: the most common route for Indian professionals in ICT, engineering, healthcare and finance. From 1 March 2026 the minimum salary is 40,904 euro (68,911 euro for roles not on the critical skills list). No labour market needs test, and after two years you can apply for Stamp 4 and work for any employer.
  • General Employment Permit: for other roles, minimum 36,605 euro from 1 March 2026, usually with a labour market needs test. Healthcare assistants and home carers have a lower threshold of 32,691 euro.
  • Study: Stamp 2 with 20 hours of work a week in term time. After a Level 8 degree the Third Level Graduate Programme gives 12 months on Stamp 1G; a Level 9 or 10 gives up to 24 months. That time is often used to find a permit sponsor.
  • Family: the spouse, de facto partner and children of a Critical Skills permit holder can apply to join immediately and the partner gets Stamp 1G, which allows work without a separate permit. Partners of General Employment Permit holders can apply after 12 months.

There is no Working Holiday scheme between Ireland and India.

Your driving licence

India is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so an Indian licence cannot be exchanged. You can drive on it for up to 12 months as a visitor if you also carry an international driving permit, but as a resident you need an Irish licence. The route is: pass the driver theory test, apply for a learner permit, complete Essential Driver Training and pass the driving test. Because you already hold a full licence you need only 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and you do not have to wait six months before sitting the test.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and India have a double taxation agreement, so income taxed in one country is credited in the other and you will not pay twice on the same salary, rental income or interest. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a calendar year. Register with Revenue through myAccount as soon as you have a PPS number so your employer does not apply emergency tax. NRI rules apply to your Indian accounts once you are non-resident in India, so convert savings accounts to NRO or NRE and tell your Indian bank.

There is no bilateral social security agreement between Ireland and India. PRSI paid in Ireland builds an Irish State Pension record but cannot be combined with EPF or NPS contributions, and vice versa.

Your Indian credit history (CIBIL) does not transfer. The Irish Central Credit Register only records Irish loans, so build a local record with a current account, a phone contract and bills in your name before applying for credit.

Healthcare

Once you are ordinarily resident (living here, or intending to, for at least a year) you can use the public system. Public hospital inpatient charges were abolished in 2023, but GP visits cost about 50 to 70 euro and waiting lists for non-urgent care are long. A medical card or GP visit card is available on income grounds. Most permit holders take private insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health, often through their employer. Take out a policy within 9 months of arriving if you are 35 or older to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading.

Bringing your things and your pet

There are no non-stop flights between Ireland and India at the time of writing; most people connect through Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Doha or London, roughly 12 to 15 hours in total. Household goods can enter free of duty under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for 12 months and owned them for 6 months.

India is an unlisted country for pet travel, so a dog or cat needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination, then a rabies antibody blood test at least 30 days after the vaccine, followed by a three month wait before the pet can enter Ireland. Add an EU animal health certificate, tapeworm treatment for dogs, and advance notice to the Department of Agriculture.

First 30 days checklist

  1. Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie with your passport, permit and proof of address.
  2. Book your IRP registration with Immigration Service Delivery within 90 days and pay the 300 euro fee.
  3. Open an Irish bank account and register with Revenue myAccount to avoid emergency tax.
  4. Register with a GP and sort private health insurance.
  5. Get a Leap card and book your driver theory test if you plan to drive.

  • Employment permits (Department of Enterprise)
  • National Driver Licence Service
  • Revenue: double taxation treaties
  • Bringing pets to Ireland

articles.title: Moving to Ireland from Brazil
articles.note: Visa-free entry, Stamp 2 language student route, no licence exchange and no tax or social security treaty.
articles.description: Brazilians are the largest non-European community in Ireland. Census 2022 counted 27,338 Brazilian citizens living here, one of the fastest growing…
articles.previewHtml:
Brazilians are the largest non-European community in Ireland. Census 2022 counted 27,338 Brazilian citizens living here, one of the fastest growing groups since 2016, and nearly 80% of them are aged between 23 and 43. The classic route is an English language course with the right to work part time, but a growing number arrive on employment permits, as students at universities, or to join a partner. This guide covers what you need to know before you fly.

Quick factsBrazil to Ireland
Visa to enterNo, up to 90 days
Registration after arrivalYes, IRP within 90 days if staying longer
Brazilian licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementNo
Social security agreementNo
Brazilian citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)27,338

Do you need a visa?

Brazilian citizens are not visa required, so you can enter Ireland for up to 90 days with a passport and, at the border, proof of your reason for coming (a course acceptance letter, an employment permit or a return ticket). To stay longer than 90 days you need an immigration permission and must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving. The main routes are:
articles.gatedHtml:
• English language student (Stamp 2): enrol on a course listed on the Interim List of Eligible Programmes of at least 25 weeks, pay in full before you travel, and show private medical insurance and funds. You can work 20 hours a week in term time and 40 hours in holidays. Each permission lasts up to 8 months and you can do a maximum of three language courses (two years), after which you must move to a higher education course to stay.
  • University or college on Stamp 2, with the Third Level Graduate Programme afterwards (12 months on Stamp 1G after a Level 8, up to 24 months after a Level 9 or 10).
  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list, minimum salary 40,904 euro from 1 March 2026, or a General Employment Permit for other roles at 36,605 euro.
  • Family: the spouse or partner of a Critical Skills permit holder gets Stamp 1G and can work without a permit; partners of Irish citizens apply for Stamp 4.

There is no Working Holiday agreement between Ireland and Brazil, so the student route remains the most common first step.

Your driving licence

Brazil is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so a CNH cannot be exchanged for an Irish licence. You can drive on your CNH with an international driving permit for up to 12 months as a visitor, but once you are resident you need to go through the Irish system: driver theory test, learner permit, Essential Driver Training and the driving test. As a full licence holder you only need 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and you can sit the test without the six month wait.

Tax, pensions and money

There is no double taxation agreement between Ireland and Brazil. Ireland taxes you on Irish income once you work here, and after 183 days in a calendar year you are Irish tax resident and taxed on worldwide income. Brazil treats you as non-resident once you file the declaração de saída definitiva with the Receita Federal, which stops Brazil taxing your Irish salary. Without a treaty, any income that both countries tax may only get partial relief, so file the exit declaration and keep records.

There is also no bilateral social security agreement, so PRSI paid in Ireland cannot be combined with INSS contributions. Your INSS record stays in Brazil and Irish PRSI builds a separate Irish State Pension record.

Your Brazilian credit history does not transfer; Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register. Open an Irish bank account or a Revolut account with an Irish IBAN as soon as you have proof of address. For real to euro transfers, specialist services are much cheaper than bank wires.

Healthcare

Students must hold private medical insurance as a condition of their permission. Once you are ordinarily resident (living here or intending to for at least a year) you can use the public HSE system: public hospital inpatient charges were abolished in 2023, but a GP visit costs around 50 to 70 euro and an Emergency Department visit without a GP referral is 100 euro. Low earners can apply for a medical card or GP visit card. If you are 35 or over, buy private insurance within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading.

Bringing your things and your pet

There are no non-stop flights between Brazil and Ireland; the usual connections are through Lisbon, Madrid, Paris, Amsterdam or London, around 14 to 16 hours in total. Most people arrive with luggage only and buy the rest here. If you do ship household goods, Transfer of Residence relief lets you import them free of duty and VAT after 12 months living outside the EU.

Brazil is an unlisted country for pet travel. Your dog or cat needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination, a rabies antibody blood test at least 30 days later at an EU approved lab, and then a three month wait before entry. You also need an EU animal health certificate, tapeworm treatment for dogs, and advance notice to the Department of Agriculture.

First 30 days checklist

  1. Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie once you have a letter confirming your address.
  2. Book your IRP registration with Immigration Service Delivery within 90 days (300 euro).
  3. Open an Irish bank account and register with Revenue myAccount to avoid emergency tax on your first payslip.
  4. Register with a GP near your accommodation.
  5. Get a Leap card, and a Student Leap card if you are on a course.

★ Useful links

  • Immigration Service Delivery
  • Coming to study in Ireland
  • Employment permits (Department of Enterprise)
  • National Driver Licence Service
  • Bringing pets to Ireland

articles.title: Moving to Ireland from South Africa
articles.appTitle: Moving to Ireland from South Africa
articles.note: Visa required since July 2024, exchangeable licence, tax treaty, rand allowances and pet titre rules.
articles.description: Census 2022 counted 8,250 South African citizens living in Ireland, plus 2,991 people with dual Irish and South African citizenship, and the community…
articles.previewHtml:
Census 2022 counted 8,250 South African citizens living in Ireland, plus 2,991 people with dual Irish and South African citizenship, and the community has kept growing since. South Africans come for jobs in tech, finance, healthcare and engineering, for the safety and the schools, and because English is the working language. The single biggest change in recent years is that South Africans now need a visa, so timing your move around the visa process matters.

Quick factsSouth Africa to Ireland
Visa to enterYes, since 10 July 2024
Registration after arrivalYes, IRP within 90 days
South African licence exchangeableYes
Double taxation agreementYes
Social security agreementNo
South African citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)8,250

Do you need a visa?

Yes. From 10 July 2024 holders of South African passports are visa required for Ireland, ending decades of visa free travel. Short visits need a C visa; a move needs a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted at a Visa Application Centre in Johannesburg, Cape Town or Durban. The visa gets you across the border; your right to stay comes from the permit or scheme behind it, and you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arrival.
articles.gatedHtml:

  • Study on Stamp 2, followed by the Third Level Graduate Programme (12 to 24 months of Stamp 1G work permission).
  • Family routes to join an Irish, EU or UK citizen spouse or partner.

If a parent or grandparent was born in Ireland, check the Foreign Births Register first: an Irish passport removes the need for any of the above. A British passport also lets you live and work in Ireland freely under the Common Travel Area. There is no Working Holiday scheme with South Africa.

Your driving licence

South Africa is on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you can exchange a full South African licence for an Irish one without a theory or driving test. You need an original letter of entitlement from the South African licensing authority, dated within six months of your application, confirming your licence categories and whether your test was in a manual or automatic car (an automatic test means an automatic only Irish licence). NDLS has flagged delays in getting these verified in South Africa, so request the letter before you leave. The exchange fee is 65 euro. You can drive on your South African licence for up to 12 months after becoming resident while the exchange goes through.

Ireland and South Africa have a double taxation agreement, so income taxed in one country is credited in the other. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a calendar year. On the South African side, decide whether to cease tax residency with SARS; the "exit charge" treats you as having sold worldwide assets on the day you leave, so get advice before the move rather than after.

There is no bilateral social security agreement. Irish PRSI and South African UIF or retirement fund contributions cannot be combined; each country pays what you have earned under its own rules.

Moving money out uses your single discretionary allowance (raised to R2 million per calendar year in the 2026 Budget) and, with a SARS tax compliance status, the R10 million foreign investment allowance. Your South African credit record does not transfer: Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so open an Irish bank account early and build a local history.

Coming from a medical aid culture, most South Africans buy private insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health. Buy it within 9 months of arriving if you are 35 or older to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading.

Bringing your things and your pet

There are no non-stop flights between South Africa and Ireland. Most people connect through London, Amsterdam, Paris, Frankfurt, Doha or Dubai, roughly 14 to 17 hours in total. Household goods you have owned for 6 months can enter free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief once you have lived outside the EU for 12 months.

South Africa is an unlisted country for pet travel. Your dog or cat needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination, then a rabies antibody blood test at least 30 days after the vaccine, and a three month wait after a successful sample before it can enter Ireland. Add an EU animal health certificate, tapeworm treatment for dogs, and advance notice to the Department of Agriculture.

  1. Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie.
  2. Book your IRP registration with Immigration Service Delivery within 90 days (300 euro).
  3. Open an Irish bank account and register with Revenue myAccount so you are not on emergency tax.
  4. Register with a GP and choose a private health insurer.
  5. Get a Leap card and submit your NDLS licence exchange while your letter of entitlement is still valid.

Census 2022 counted 8,250 South African citizens living in Ireland, plus 2,991 people with dual Irish and South African citizenship, and the community has kept growing since. South Africans come for jobs in tech, finance, healthcare and engineering, for the safety and the schools, and because English is the working language. The single biggest change in recent years is that South Africans now need a visa, so timing your move around the visa process matters.

Quick factsSouth Africa to IrelandVisa to enterYes, since 10 July 2024Registration after arrivalYes, IRP within 90 daysSouth African licence exchangeableYesDouble taxation agreementYesSocial security agreementNoSouth African citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)8,250

Do you need a visa?

Yes. From 10 July 2024 holders of South African passports are visa required for Ireland, ending decades of visa free travel. Short visits need a C visa; a move needs a long stay D visa, applied for online through AVATS and submitted at a Visa Application Centre in Johannesburg, Cape Town or Durban. The visa gets you across the border; your right to stay comes from the permit or scheme behind it, and you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arrival.

Critical Skills Employment Permit for roles on the critical skills list (ICT, engineering, nursing, doctors, accountants and more). Minimum salary 40,904 euro from 1 March 2026, or 68,911 euro for other eligible jobs. No labour market needs test. Your spouse or partner can join you straight away on Stamp 1G and work without a permit.General Employment Permit for other jobs at 36,605 euro (32,691 euro for healthcare assistants and home carers), usually after a labour market needs test.Study on Stamp 2, followed by the Third Level Graduate Programme (12 to 24 months of Stamp 1G work permission).Family routes to join an Irish, EU or UK citizen spouse or partner.

If a parent or grandparent was born in Ireland, check the Foreign Births Register first: an Irish passport removes the need for any of the above. A British passport also lets you live and work in Ireland freely under the Common Travel Area. There is no Working Holiday scheme with South Africa.

Your driving licence

South Africa is on the NDLS list of recognised states, so you can exchange a full South African licence for an Irish one without a theory or driving test. You need an original letter of entitlement from the South African licensing authority, dated within six months of your application, confirming your licence categories and whether your test was in a manual or automatic car (an automatic test means an automatic only Irish licence). NDLS has flagged delays in getting these verified in South Africa, so request the letter before you leave. The exchange fee is 65 euro. You can drive on your South African licence for up to 12 months after becoming resident while the exchange goes through.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and South Africa have a double taxation agreement, so income taxed in one country is credited in the other. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a calendar year. On the South African side, decide whether to cease tax residency with SARS; the "exit charge" treats you as having sold worldwide assets on the day you leave, so get advice before the move rather than after.

There is no bilateral social security agreement. Irish PRSI and South African UIF or retirement fund contributions cannot be combined; each country pays what you have earned under its own rules.

Moving money out uses your single discretionary allowance (raised to R2 million per calendar year in the 2026 Budget) and, with a SARS tax compliance status, the R10 million foreign investment allowance. Your South African credit record does not transfer: Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so open an Irish bank account early and build a local history.

Healthcare

Your visa application must include private medical insurance. Once you are ordinarily resident (living here or intending to for at least a year) you can use the public HSE system. Public hospital inpatient charges were abolished in 2023, but GP visits cost roughly 50 to 70 euro and waiting lists for non-urgent care are long. Coming from a medical aid culture, most South Africans buy private insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health. Buy it within 9 months of arriving if you are 35 or older to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading.

Bringing your things and your pet

There are no non-stop flights between South Africa and Ireland. Most people connect through London, Amsterdam, Paris, Frankfurt, Doha or Dubai, roughly 14 to 17 hours in total. Household goods you have owned for 6 months can enter free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief once you have lived outside the EU for 12 months.

South Africa is an unlisted country for pet travel. Your dog or cat needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination, then a rabies antibody blood test at least 30 days after the vaccine, and a three month wait after a successful sample before it can enter Ireland. Add an EU animal health certificate, tapeworm treatment for dogs, and advance notice to the Department of Agriculture.

Census 2022 counted 8,368 Nigerian citizens and a further 8,085 people with dual Irish and Nigerian citizenship, with over 20,000 residents born in Nigeria. People come for nursing, medicine, IT and engineering jobs, for postgraduate study, and to join family. This guide covers the paperwork, the money and the practical realities.

Visa to enterYes (long stay D visa)
Registration after arrivalYes, IRP within 90 days
Nigerian licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementNo
Social security agreementNo
Nigerian citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)8,368 (plus 8,085 dual)

Yes. Nigerian citizens are visa required. For a move you apply online through AVATS for a long stay D visa and submit your passport and documents through the visa application centre in Abuja or Lagos. Give yourself time: Irish visa decisions for Nigeria have historically taken longer than average, and refusals are common where documents are incomplete, so follow the checklist for your visa type exactly and show clear evidence of funds. articles.gatedHtml:
• Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list, including nurses, doctors, engineers and many ICT roles. Minimum salary 40,904 euro from 1 March 2026 (68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Your spouse or partner and children can apply to join you immediately and the partner gets Stamp 1G, which allows work without a permit.
  • General Employment Permit for other roles at 36,605 euro, or 32,691 euro for healthcare assistants and home carers, usually after a labour market needs test.
  • Study on Stamp 2. Postgraduate courses are popular because a Level 9 degree leads to up to 24 months on Stamp 1G under the Third Level Graduate Programme, during which you can work full time for any employer.
  • Family reunification to join an Irish citizen or a permit holder, and the parent of an Irish citizen child route.

There is no Working Holiday scheme with Nigeria.

Your driving licence

Nigeria is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so a Nigerian licence cannot be exchanged. You may drive on it with an international driving permit for up to 12 months as a visitor, but as a resident you need an Irish licence: driver theory test, learner permit, Essential Driver Training and the driving test. Because you already hold a full licence held for at least two years you qualify for the reduced programme of 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and you can sit the test without waiting six months.

Tax, pensions and money

There is no double taxation agreement in effect between Ireland and Nigeria. Once you live and work in Ireland you pay Irish PAYE, USC and PRSI on your salary, and after 183 days in a calendar year you are Irish tax resident. Nigerian income you keep, such as rent, may be taxed in Nigeria under Nigerian rules; without a treaty, relief for any double tax is limited, so keep records and get advice if you have significant Nigerian income.

There is also no bilateral social security agreement. Irish PRSI builds a separate Irish State Pension record and cannot be combined with your Nigerian pension (RSA) contributions.

Your Nigerian credit history does not transfer. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so open an Irish bank account as soon as you have proof of address and build a record with a phone contract and bills in your name. Bringing savings from Nigeria is the hard part: naira to euro transfers are limited by Nigerian banks' foreign exchange rules, so plan them well before you travel and use licensed channels.

Healthcare

Your visa application must include private medical insurance for your first period. Once you are ordinarily resident (living here or intending to for at least a year) you can use the public HSE system. Public hospital inpatient charges were abolished in 2023, but GP visits cost about 50 to 70 euro, an Emergency Department visit without a GP referral is 100 euro, and non-urgent waiting lists are long. Low earners can apply for a medical card or GP visit card. Many permit holders take private insurance through their employer; if you are 35 or older, take out a policy within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading.

Bringing your things and your pet

There are no non-stop flights between Nigeria and Ireland. The usual connections from Lagos or Abuja are through London, Paris, Amsterdam, Istanbul or Addis Ababa, around 9 to 13 hours in total. Household goods you have owned for 6 months can enter free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief once you have lived outside the EU for 12 months.

Nigeria is an unlisted country for pet travel. A dog or cat needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination, a rabies antibody blood test at least 30 days later at an EU approved laboratory, and then a three month wait before it can enter. You also need an EU animal health certificate, tapeworm treatment for dogs, and advance notice to the Department of Agriculture.

First 30 days checklist

  1. Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie with your passport, permit and proof of address.
  2. Book your IRP registration with Immigration Service Delivery within 90 days (300 euro).
  3. Open an Irish bank account and register with Revenue myAccount to avoid emergency tax.
  4. Register with a GP and check whether you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card.
  5. Get a Leap card and book your driver theory test if you plan to drive.

  • National Driver Licence Service
  • Citizens Information: entitlement to health services
  • Bringing pets to Ireland

articles.title: Moving to Ireland from Canada
articles.note: Two-year Working Holiday Authorisation, licence exchange for seven provinces, CPP and OAS abroad.
articles.description: Census 2022 counted 3,528 Canadian citizens living in Ireland, plus 5,855 people with dual Irish and Canadian citizenship. Canadians come for the two…
articles.previewHtml:
Census 2022 counted 3,528 Canadian citizens living in Ireland, plus 5,855 people with dual Irish and Canadian citizenship. Canadians come for the two year Working Holiday Authorisation, for jobs in tech, finance and healthcare, for university, or to reclaim an Irish passport through a parent or grandparent. Here is what you need to sort out.

Quick factsCanada to Ireland
Visa to enterNo, up to 90 days
Working Holiday AuthorisationYes, ages 18 to 35, up to 2 years
Canadian licence exchangeableYes, from 7 provinces only
Double taxation agreementYes
Social security agreementYes (Canada, and a separate one with Quebec)
Canadian citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)3,528 (plus 5,855 dual)

Do you need a visa?

Canadian citizens are not visa required, so you enter Ireland for up to 90 days with just a passport. To stay longer you need an immigration permission and must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arrival. The main routes:
articles.gatedHtml:
• Working Holiday Authorisation: Canadians aged 18 to 35 can live and work in Ireland for up to 2 years, the longest stay Ireland offers any working holiday nationality. You do not need a job offer. Apply directly to the Embassy of Ireland in Ottawa or through SWAP Working Holidays; the fee is 150 Canadian dollars. You need proof of funds, health insurance and a return ticket or funds for one.
  • Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list, minimum salary 40,904 euro from 1 March 2026 (68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Partners get Stamp 1G and can work without their own permit.
  • General Employment Permit for other jobs at 36,605 euro, usually after a labour market needs test.
  • Study on Stamp 2, with the Third Level Graduate Programme afterwards.
  • Family routes to join an Irish or EU citizen spouse or partner.

Many Canadians have an Irish born grandparent. If you do, apply to the Foreign Births Register: once registered you are an Irish citizen and need no permission at all.

Your driving licence

Canada is on the NDLS list of recognised states, but only for licences issued by Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Ontario and Saskatchewan. Licences from Quebec, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island and the territories cannot be exchanged. If yours qualifies, you exchange it at the NDLS for 65 euro with no test; you may need a driver abstract from your province, and only the car category is exchanged in most cases. If yours does not qualify, you can drive on it for up to 12 months as a visitor, then must pass the theory test, take a learner permit, complete 6 EDT lessons (reduced from 12 for experienced drivers) and pass the driving test.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and Canada have a double taxation agreement. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a calendar year, and the treaty decides which country taxes what. Tell the CRA when you leave and consider whether you are severing Canadian residency, which triggers departure tax on some assets. On a working holiday you are usually taxed only on your Irish earnings; claim any refund through Revenue myAccount when you leave.

Ireland has bilateral social security agreements with Canada (since 1992) and separately with Quebec. They let you combine CPP or QPP contribution periods with Irish PRSI to qualify for a pension in either country. CPP is paid anywhere in the world once you qualify. OAS needs 20 years of Canadian residence after age 18 to be paid indefinitely abroad, and time in Ireland can count towards that threshold under the agreement.

Your Canadian credit history does not transfer. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so open an Irish bank account or a Revolut account with an Irish IBAN once you have proof of address.

Healthcare

Working holiday applicants must show private health insurance. Once you are ordinarily resident (living here or intending to for at least a year) you can use the public HSE system. Unlike provincial health plans, the HSE charges for GP visits (about 50 to 70 euro) unless you qualify for a medical card or GP visit card; public hospital inpatient charges were abolished in 2023. Around half the population holds private insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health. If you are 35 or older, buy it within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading.

Bringing your things and your pet

Air Canada flies non-stop from Toronto and Vancouver and the journey is 6 to 9 hours, so most working holiday makers arrive with two suitcases. If you ship household goods, they enter free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for 12 months and owned them for 6 months.

Canada is a listed country for pet travel, so your dog or cat does not need a rabies blood test. It needs an ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination given after the chip, an EU animal health certificate endorsed by the CFIA, tapeworm treatment for dogs, and you must give the Department of Agriculture advance notice so a compliance check can be done on arrival.

First 30 days checklist

  1. Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie once you have a letter confirming your Irish address.
  2. Book your IRP registration with Immigration Service Delivery within 90 days (300 euro).
  3. Open an Irish bank account and register with Revenue myAccount so your first payslip is not on emergency tax.
  4. Register with a GP and decide on private health insurance.
  5. Get a Leap card and, if your province qualifies, exchange your licence at the NDLS.

★ Useful links

  • Embassy of Ireland, Ottawa: Working Holiday Programme
  • Immigration Service Delivery
  • National Driver Licence Service
  • Bilateral social security agreements
  • Foreign Births Register

articles.previewHtml:
Census 2022 counted 3,481 Australian citizens living in Ireland and a much larger 14,444 people with dual Irish and Australian citizenship, one of the biggest dual citizen groups in the country. Australians come for the 12 month Working Holiday Authorisation, for jobs in tech, finance, construction and healthcare, to reconnect with family, or to use Ireland as a base for Europe. Here is what to expect.

Quick factsAustralia to Ireland
Visa to enterNo, up to 90 days

Do you need a visa?

Australian citizens are not visa required and can enter Ireland for up to 90 days on a passport alone. To stay longer you need an immigration permission and must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arrival. The main routes:
articles.gatedHtml:

  • General Employment Permit for other jobs at 36,605 euro, usually after a labour market needs test.
  • Study on Stamp 2 with the Third Level Graduate Programme afterwards.
  • Family routes to join an Irish or EU citizen spouse or partner.

Your driving licence

Australia is on the NDLS list of recognised states, so a full Australian licence from any state or territory can be exchanged for an Irish licence with no theory or driving test.   4. Register with a GP and decide on private health insurance.

articles.plainText:
Census 2022 counted 3,481 Australian citizens living in Ireland and a much larger 14,444 people with dual Irish and Australian citizenship, one of the biggest dual citizen groups in the country. Australians come for the 12 month Working Holiday Authorisation, for jobs in tech, finance, construction and healthcare, to reconnect with family, or to use Ireland as a base for Europe. Here is what to expect.

Quick factsAustralia to IrelandVisa to enterNo, up to 90 daysWorking Holiday AuthorisationYes, ages 18 to 35, 12 monthsAustralian licence exchangeableYesDouble taxation agreementYesSocial security agreementYes (since 1992)Australian citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)3,481 (plus 14,444 dual)

Do you need a visa?

Australian citizens are not visa required and can enter Ireland for up to 90 days on a passport alone. To stay longer you need an immigration permission and must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arrival. The main routes:

Working Holiday Authorisation: Australians aged 18 to 35 can live and work in Ireland for 12 months from the date of entry. You cannot work for a single employer for more than 6 months, and you do not need a job offer. Apply through the Embassy of Ireland in Canberra; the processing fee is 95 Australian dollars. You need proof of funds, health insurance and a return ticket or the funds for one.Critical Skills Employment Permit for jobs on the critical skills list, minimum salary 40,904 euro from 1 March 2026 (68,911 euro for other eligible roles). Partners get Stamp 1G and can work without a permit of their own.General Employment Permit for other jobs at 36,605 euro, usually after a labour market needs test.Study on Stamp 2 with the Third Level Graduate Programme afterwards.Family routes to join an Irish or EU citizen spouse or partner.

Given how many Australians have Irish grandparents, check the Foreign Births Register first. Registration makes you an Irish citizen with full EU rights and takes roughly 9 to 12 months.

Your driving licence

Australia is on the NDLS list of recognised states, so a full Australian licence from any state or territory can be exchanged for an Irish licence with no theory or driving test. Apply online at ndls.ie or at an NDLS centre with your licence, proof of PPS number, proof of address and photo ID; the fee is 65 euro. Not every category transfers, and NDLS may ask for a letter of entitlement from your state licensing authority, so request one before you leave. Exchange it within 1 year of its expiry date at the latest.

Tax, pensions and money

Ireland and Australia have a double taxation agreement. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a calendar year, and the treaty decides which country taxes what. Tell the ATO whether you are ceasing Australian residency; if you keep Australian rental income it stays taxable there.

Ireland has had a bilateral social security agreement with Australia since 1992 (revised in 2006). It lets you add Australian working life residence to Irish PRSI contributions to qualify for a pension in either country, each paying a pro rata share. The Age Pension can be paid in Ireland, and Services Australia pays it in euro into an Irish account. Your superannuation stays in Australia until preservation age unless you were only ever a temporary resident, in which case you may claim a Departing Australia Superannuation Payment after leaving, taxed at 35% to 65% depending on your visa.

Your Australian credit history does not transfer; Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register. Open an Irish bank account or a Revolut account with an Irish IBAN as soon as you have proof of address.

Healthcare

Working holiday applicants must show private health insurance. Once you are ordinarily resident (living here or intending to for at least a year) you can use the public HSE system. Compared with Medicare, the main difference is that GP visits cost about 50 to 70 euro unless you have a medical card or GP visit card; public hospital inpatient charges were abolished in 2023. Australia has a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Ireland covering emergency and necessary treatment for visitors, but as a resident you should either take private insurance from VHI, Laya or Irish Life Health or budget for GP fees. If you are 35 or older, buy insurance within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading.

Bringing your things and your pet

There are no non-stop flights between Australia and Ireland. One stop via Dubai, Doha, Abu Dhabi or Singapore takes 21 to 25 hours in total. If you do ship, household goods enter free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief if you have lived outside the EU for 12 months and owned them for 6 months.

Australia is a listed country for pet travel, so your dog or cat does not need a rabies blood test. It needs an ISO microchip, a rabies vaccination given after the chip and at least 21 days before travel, an EU animal health certificate endorsed by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry, tapeworm treatment for dogs, and advance notice to the Irish Department of Agriculture for a compliance check on arrival.

First 30 days checklist

Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie once you have a letter confirming your Irish address.Book your IRP registration with Immigration Service Delivery within 90 days (300 euro).Open an Irish bank account and register with Revenue myAccount to avoid emergency tax.Register with a GP and decide on private health insurance.Get a Leap card and exchange your licence at the NDLS.

articles.title: Moving to Ireland from the Philippines
articles.appTitle: Moving to Ireland from the Philippines
articles.note: Nursing route via NMBI, Atypical Working Scheme and Critical Skills permits, D visa, no tax treaty.
articles.description: Census 2022 counted 7,736 Filipino citizens living in Ireland and a further 3,319 people with dual Irish and Filipino citizenship. The community is…
articles.previewHtml:
Census 2022 counted 7,736 Filipino citizens living in Ireland and a further 3,319 people with dual Irish and Filipino citizenship. The community is closely tied to healthcare: Filipino nurses, midwives, care assistants and doctors have staffed Irish hospitals and nursing homes for over two decades, and the HSE and private providers still recruit directly from the Philippines.

Quick factsPhilippines to Ireland
Visa to enterYes (long stay D visa)
Registration after arrivalYes, IRP within 90 days
Philippine licence exchangeableNo
Double taxation agreementNo (under negotiation)
Social security agreementNo
Filipino citizens in Ireland (Census 2022)7,736 (plus 3,319 dual)

Do you need a visa?

Yes. Filipino citizens are visa required. For a move you apply online through AVATS for a long stay D visa and lodge your passport and documents through the visa application centre in Manila or Cebu. The visa lets you enter; your right to stay comes from the employment permit or scheme behind it, and you must register for an Irish Residence Permit (300 euro) within 90 days of arriving. The main routes:
articles.gatedHtml:
• Nursing and midwifery: first apply to the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Ireland (NMBI) for recognition of your qualification. Most overseas nurses are then asked to complete an aptitude test or a supervised clinical adaptation placement of 6 to 12 weeks in an Irish hospital. You come for that stage on the Atypical Working Scheme, and once registered your employer applies for a Critical Skills Employment Permit. Nurses are on the critical skills list, so no labour market needs test is needed, and from 1 March 2026 the minimum salary for nurses is 40,904 euro (36,848 euro if you qualified in the last 12 months). Realistically the whole process takes 9 to 18 months.
  • Healthcare assistants and home carers: a General Employment Permit with a lower threshold of 32,691 euro from 1 March 2026, usually after a labour market needs test.
  • Family: the spouse or partner and children of a Critical Skills permit holder can apply to join you immediately, and the partner gets Stamp 1G and can work without a separate permit.

On the Philippine side you must leave through a Department of Migrant Workers accredited agency or a DMW registered direct hire, and get an Overseas Employment Certificate before departure, or you will be stopped at the airport. There is no Working Holiday scheme between Ireland and the Philippines.

Your driving licence

The Philippines is not on the NDLS list of recognised states, so an LTO licence cannot be exchanged. You can drive on it with an international driving permit for up to 12 months as a visitor, but as a resident you need an Irish licence: driver theory test, learner permit, Essential Driver Training and the driving test. Because you already hold a full licence you need only 6 EDT lessons instead of 12 and can sit the test without the six month wait.

Tax, pensions and money

There is no double taxation agreement in effect between Ireland and the Philippines; negotiations began in 2019 but nothing has been signed. In practice this rarely matters for salaried workers because the Philippines does not tax the foreign income of non-resident citizens, and Ireland taxes your Irish salary through PAYE, USC and PRSI. You become Irish tax resident after 183 days in a calendar year.

There is no bilateral social security agreement, so Irish PRSI cannot be combined with SSS or GSIS contributions. Your SSS record stays in the Philippines and you can keep paying voluntarily as an OFW if you want to protect it; Irish PRSI builds a separate Irish State Pension entitlement.

Your Philippine credit history does not transfer. Irish lenders only see the Central Credit Register, so open an Irish bank account early and build a record with bills and a phone contract in your name.

Healthcare

Your visa application must include private medical insurance. Once you are ordinarily resident (living here or intending to for at least a year) you can use the public HSE system. Public hospital inpatient charges were abolished in 2023, but GP visits cost about 50 to 70 euro unless you have a medical card or GP visit card, which are means tested. HSE employees usually get access to discounted group health insurance schemes; if you are 35 or older, take out a policy within 9 months of arriving to avoid a Lifetime Community Rating loading.

Bringing your things and your pet

There are no non-stop flights between the Philippines and Ireland. Most people fly Manila to Dublin via Doha, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Istanbul or London, around 17 to 20 hours in total. Household goods you have owned for 6 months can enter free of duty and VAT under Transfer of Residence relief once you have lived outside the EU for 12 months.

The Philippines is an unlisted country for pet travel. A dog or cat needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination, a rabies antibody blood test at least 30 days later at an EU approved laboratory, and then a three month wait before entry. You also need an EU animal health certificate, tapeworm treatment for dogs, and advance notice to the Department of Agriculture.

First 30 days checklist

  1. Apply for a PPS number through MyWelfare.ie with your passport, permit and proof of address.
  2. Book your IRP registration with Immigration Service Delivery within 90 days (300 euro).
  3. Open an Irish bank account and register with Revenue myAccount so you are not on emergency tax.
  4. Register with a GP and sort health insurance through your employer if offered.
  5. Get a Leap card and book your driver theory test if you plan to drive.

★ Useful links

  • Immigration Service Delivery
  • NMBI: nurses qualified outside the EU
  • Employment permits (Department of Enterprise)
  • National Driver Licence Service
  • Citizens Information: entitlement to health services

articles.title: Minimum standards for moving with a pet
articles.appTitle: Minimum standards for moving with a pet
articles.description: Bringing a pet along while relocating to Ireland can be a complex process, and there are several things that you will need to take care of in order to…
articles.previewHtml:
Bringing a pet along while relocating to Ireland can be a complex process, and there are several things that you will need to take care of in order to ensure that your pet can enter the country and be properly cared for:

Be microchipped: This must be done before anything else.

Pet passport: Pets will need a pet passport, which will need to be issued by a veterinarian in their home country. The passport will need to include information such as the pet's microchip number, vaccination records, and details of any recent treatments.
articles.gatedHtml:
Rabies vaccination: Pets will need to have a current rabies vaccination, and it is advisable that this is done at least 21 days before travel.

Tapeworm treatment: Dogs will need to have been treated for tapeworms not less than 24 hours and not more than 120 hours (1-5 days) before the scheduled arrival time in Ireland.

Blood test: Pets that are coming from certain countries will need to have a blood test to show that they have sufficient rabies antibody levels.

Import license: Some pets will require an import license, which must be obtained from the Irish Department of Agriculture, Food, and the Marine.

Quarantine: Pets coming from certain countries may need to be quarantined for a period of time upon arrival in Ireland.

Accommodation and care: You will need to make arrangements for the accommodation and care of their pet while you are in Ireland. This could include finding a pet-friendly hotel or rental property, or making arrangements with a pet-sitting service.

Familiarize with the pet laws: It's important to familiarize yourself with the pet laws and regulations in Ireland, and make sure that you can comply with them.

★ Tip

  • Vets who specialize in international travel who can help with the paperwork.

It's significant to note that the pet's needs and regulations may vary depending on the pet's breed, size, and health condition, and it is always advisable to check with the Irish embassy or consulate in your home country or with the Irish Department of Agriculture, Food, and the Marine for the most up-to-date information on pet importation requirements.

★ Useful links

  1. Pet travel page from: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine
  2. Dog licenses and ownership

articles.title: Pet ownership in Ireland
articles.description: Pet ownership in Ireland is a popular and cherished pastime, with many households welcoming furry friends into their homes. Whether it's a dog, cat, or…
articles.previewHtml: Pet ownership in Ireland is a popular and cherished pastime, with many households welcoming furry friends into their homes. Whether it's a dog, cat, or rabbit, pets are an important part of the Irish family and culture. However, owning a pet in Ireland also comes with certain responsibilities and regulations that pet owners must abide by.
articles.gatedHtml:
First and foremost, all dogs in Ireland must be microchipped and registered with the local authority. This is a legal requirement and failure to comply can result in fines or penalties. Microchipping is a quick and simple process that involves inserting a small chip under the dog's skin, which contains identifying information about the dog and its owner. This is a useful tool for reuniting lost or stolen dogs with their owners.

In addition to microchipping, dogs must also be vaccinated against certain diseases, including rabies. The vaccination must be done by a veterinarian and the dog must have an up-to-date vaccination certificate. Dogs are also required to be treated for tapeworms not less than 24 hours and not more than 120 hours (1-5 days) before the scheduled arrival time in Ireland.

Pet owners must also ensure that their pets are well cared for and not causing a nuisance to others. This includes providing them with adequate food and water, as well as a clean and safe environment to live in. Pet owners are also responsible for cleaning up after their pets in public places, and failure to do so can result in fines.

Ireland has a strict policy regarding the breeding of dogs. It is illegal to breed dogs without a license, and all breeding establishments must be registered with the local authority. This is to ensure that breeding is done responsibly, and that puppies are healthy and well-cared for.

Overall, pet ownership in Ireland is a rewarding experience that brings joy and companionship to many families. However, it is important for pet owners to understand and comply with the regulations in place to ensure the welfare of their pets and the safety of the community. By being responsible and informed pet owners, we can continue to foster the strong bond between humans and their animal companions in Ireland.

articles.title: Getting here I: Airlines
articles.description: Moving to a new country with a pet can be a challenging process, but with the right preparation and information, it can be a smooth and stress-free…
articles.previewHtml: Moving to a new country with a pet can be a challenging process, but with the right preparation and information, it can be a smooth and stress-free experience. If you are moving to Ireland with your pet, it's important to understand the airport rules, airline selection, and the necessary steps involved in transporting your furry friend.
articles.gatedHtml:
Airlines

When selecting an airline, it's significant to choose one that has a good reputation for handling pets and has clear and comprehensive policies in place. Some airlines have restrictions on the size and type of pet carrier, so make sure to check this beforehand. Furthermore, be sure to book your pet's flight as early as possible, as there are often limited spaces available for pets on flights.

Most airlines do not allow administering sedatives to dogs during travel, as it could lead to breathing difficulties or even fatalities in the cargo area.

Additionally, many airlines also ban brachiocephalic breeds, such as boxers, bulldogs, sharpeis, shih tzus, pugs, and so on, for similar reasons. It's best to check with your airline to confirm their policies.

Check the rules on airline web page, for instance:

- Aer Lingus:

https://www.aerlingus.com/prepare/bags/travelling-with-pets/

- Turkish Airlines:

https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-int/any-questions/traveling-with-pets/

- American Airlines:
https://www.aa.com/i18n/travel-info/special-assistance/pets.jsp

articles.title: Getting here II: Airports
articles.description: When it comes to airport rules, it's essential to familiarize yourself with the regulations regarding pet transport. This includes information about…
articles.previewHtml:
When it comes to airport rules, it's essential to familiarize yourself with the regulations regarding pet transport. This includes information about check-in procedures, pet-friendly facilities, and restrictions on the types of pet carriers allowed in the cabin or as cargo. You should also be prepared for additional security checks, especially if your pet is travelling as cargo.

It's also significant to prepare your pet for the journey. This includes acclimatizing them to their pet carrier, providing them with food and water, and making sure they are comfortable and relaxed during the flight. You should also consider hiring a pet-friendly travel agent or consultant who can help you navigate the process and ensure that everything runs smoothly.
articles.gatedHtml:
To enter the Republic of Ireland, travellers must pass through compliance checks upon arrival at one of the following ports of entry:

  • Cork Airport
  • Dublin Airport
  • Dublin Port
  • Shannon Airport
  • Port of Cork at Ringaskiddy
  • Rosslare Europort

Compliance Requirements for Non-EU Pets

If a pet is travelling from a non-European Union country to Ireland, it must enter through Cork, Dublin, Shannon Airport, or Cork or Rosslare Port and undergo compliance checks upon arrival. The pet owner is responsible for ensuring that the pet undergoes the necessary checks, and must arrange for them ahead of the pet's arrival.

To initiate the process, the pet owner must send a notice form to the relevant email address, as follows:

Dublin airport: petmove@agriculture.gov.ie

Cork airport: corkpetmove@agriculture.gov.ie

Shannon airport: petsshannon@agriculture.gov.ie

Ringaskiddy port, Cork: corkpetmove@agriculture.gov.ie

Rosslare ferry port: rosslare.europort@agriculture.gov.ie

The form should include the following information:

Date and time of arrival

Airport or port

Owner's name

Flight number (if applicable)

Number of animals to be checked

Travel paperwork, such as an EU Pet Passport or an EU (Annex IV) Health Certificate

There is a fee for compliance checks, which may be performed at the airport or port of arrival, or at the quarantine facility located at Lissenhall Veterinary Hospital, approximately 10 km from Dublin airport.

In conclusion, moving to Ireland with a pet requires careful planning and preparation. By understanding the airport rules, airline selection, and the necessary steps involved in transporting your pet, you can make the process as stress-free as possible for both you and your furry friend. With a little effort and attention to detail, you can ensure that your pet has a safe and comfortable journey to their new home in Ireland.

Number of animals to be checked

Travel paperwork, such as an EU Pet Passport or an EU (Annex IV) Health Certificate

By understanding the airport rules, airline selection, and the necessary steps involved in transporting your pet, you can make the process as stress-free as possible for both you and your furry friend. With a little effort and attention to detail, you can ensure that your pet has a safe and comfortable journey to their new home in Ireland.

articles.title: Your top priority: Apply for PPS number
articles.appTitle: Your top priority: Apply for PPS number
articles.description: PPS (Personal Public Service) Number is an important document for anyone who moves to Ireland, as it serves as a unique identifier for accessing public…
articles.previewHtml:
PPS (Personal Public Service) Number is an important document for anyone who moves to Ireland, as it serves as a unique identifier for accessing public services and benefits in the country.

What is it used for?

The PPS number is used for a variety of purposes in Ireland, including applying for social welfare benefits, paying taxes, and accessing healthcare services. It is a crucial document that allows you to participate in the Irish social welfare system and receive benefits and services that you may be entitled to.

Documents needed to apply

To apply for a PPS number, you need to provide a range of documentation, including proof of identity, proof of address, and proof of your right to reside in Ireland. This may include your passport, visa, or work permit, as well as a recent utility bill or bank statement to confirm your address. You may also need to provide evidence of your employment status and your eligibility for benefits and services in Ireland.
articles.gatedHtml:
Proof of Address

In Ireland, the following documents are generally accepted as proof of address:

  • Utility bill (e.g., electricity, gas, or water bill)
  • Bank statement
  • Rental agreement
  • Correspondence from a government agency (e.g., Social Welfare, Revenue Commissioners)
  • A letter from an employer or educational institution

Potential consequences if you don't get it in time

If you do not obtain a PPS number in a timely manner, you may face several potential consequences. This can include being unable to access certain benefits and services, such as healthcare, and being unable to participate in the Irish social welfare system. Furthermore, you may also face difficulties opening a bank account, accessing credit, and paying taxes.

★ Important info

  • You will be paying Emergency Tax rates until you have a PPS number. This is why getting a PPS number should be your priority.

Can you apply for PPS Number if you are living outside Ireland?

The short answer is yes, it is possible! Long answer:

If you are living outside Ireland and require a PPS Number for an interaction with a specified body in Ireland such as the Office of the Revenue Commissioners for reasons such as Taxation, Probate and the buying of property, you need to complete an application form Application form for a PPS Number (REG1) and also provide the following:

  • Evidence of your address
  • Proof of your identity
  • Proof of reason for why a PPS Number is required
  • PPS Number Exceptional Registration Application Form
  • Consent form signed by you if the PPS Number is to be given to a third-party representative, for example, a solicitor or accountant
  • Questionnaire

Completed forms should be emailed to CIS@welfare.ie or posted to;

Department of Social Protection,

Shannon Lodge,

Carrick on Shannon,

Co. Leitrim, N41 KD81,

Republic of Ireland.

Average taking time

The process of obtaining a PPS number in Ireland can take many weeks, depending on the volume of applications and the complexity of your individual case. It is important to apply for your PPS number as soon as you arrive in Ireland, as this will help ensure that you can access the benefits and services you are entitled to in a timely manner.

In conclusion

The PPS number is a critical document for anyone who moves to Ireland, as it is used to access public services and benefits in the country. To apply for a PPS number, you need to provide proof of identity, address, and your right to reside in Ireland. Failure to obtain a PPS number in a timely manner can result in difficulties accessing benefits and services, and participating in the Irish social welfare system. The average processing time for a PPS number is several weeks.
