articles.title: Third-level education
articles.description: Third level education in Ireland is highly regarded and recognized worldwide, with a range of courses available across universities, institutes of…
articles.previewHtml:
Third level education in Ireland is highly regarded and recognized worldwide, with a range of courses available across universities, institutes of technology, and colleges of education. There are over 30 higher education institutions in the country, offering both undergraduate and postgraduate programs.

Undergraduate courses typically last three to four years, and students can choose from a range of disciplines, including arts, science, engineering, medicine, law, and more. To gain entry to these courses, students need to have completed their secondary school education and obtained a Leaving Certificate.
articles.gatedHtml:
The Leaving Certificate is a state examination taken by students at the end of their secondary education, usually when they are 18 years old. It is the main route of entry to higher education in Ireland and is accepted by universities and colleges both in Ireland and abroad. The Leaving Certificate results are measured on a points system, with students being awarded points based on their performance in six subjects.

For those who do not have the Leaving Certificate or who did not achieve the necessary results, there are other ways to gain entry to third level education in Ireland. One option is to undertake a Post Leaving Certificate (PLC) course, which can provide students with the necessary skills and knowledge to progress to a third level course.

Postgraduate courses are also available in Ireland, with options ranging from taught Masters programs to research-based PhDs. To gain entry to these courses, students usually need to have completed an undergraduate degree in a related field.

Higher education in Ireland is funded by the government, with tuition fees being lower for Irish and EU students than for those from outside the EU. Students may also be eligible for financial assistance in the form of grants or scholarships, depending on their circumstances.

Overall, Ireland offers a high-quality education system, with a range of options available to suit the needs and interests of students at all levels. With its strong reputation and international recognition, a qualification from an Irish higher education institution can open up a range of exciting career opportunities for graduates.

articles.title: Register your child to school
articles.description: If you have moved to Ireland with school-age children, there are certain steps you need to take to ensure they are enrolled in school and receive a…
articles.previewHtml:
If you have moved to Ireland with school-age children, there are certain steps you need to take to ensure they are enrolled in school and receive a quality education. Here's what you need to know:

Research Schools: Do some research on the schools in your area, including primary schools, secondary schools, and any other education options available. Consider factors such as location, school size, academic performance, and extracurricular activities.
articles.gatedHtml:
Register Your Child: Once you have identified the school you want your child to attend, contact the school and register your child. This will usually involve completing an application form and providing proof of address and your child's birth certificate.

Ensure You Meet Admission Requirements: Admission requirements vary between schools, so make sure you are aware of any specific requirements for the school you have chosen. Some schools have waiting lists, so it's important to register your child as early as possible.

School Curriculum: The Irish school system is divided into primary and secondary education, with a strong emphasis on the core subjects of English, mathematics, and science. Primary education covers ages 4-12, while secondary education covers ages 12-18. Make sure you understand the curriculum and what your child will be learning in each year.

School Uniforms: Many schools in Ireland have a dress code or uniform policy. Be sure to check with the school on their uniform policy and where to purchase the necessary clothing.

Fees: Primary and secondary education is free in Ireland for Irish and EU citizens. Non-EU citizens may be required to pay fees for education. It's important to check with the school on any fees that may be applicable.

Transport: Some schools offer transportation services for students, while others may require students to travel to and from school on their own. Consider the distance between your home and the school, and make arrangements as necessary.

Overall, the Irish education system is highly regarded for its quality and emphasis on academic achievement. By following these steps and doing your research, you can ensure your child receives a quality education and a successful transition to life in Ireland.
